best_plan.name: p2
best_plan.rationale: p2 achieved the best observed quality among valid plans (f1_score 0.947) while keeping cost and latency moderate on rerun ($0.00525, 7.10s). It beats p4 on quality by a wide margin, and it beats p3 by being both cheaper and much more accurate; p1 was not a reliable final choice because evaluation failed.

plan_codes.p1:
left = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name + "_left", "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
left.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")

right = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name + "_right", "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
right.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")

joined = left.sem_join(
    right,
    "the two reviews express the same overall sentiment about the movie (both positive or both negative), and they are different reviews",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE
)
joined.limit(10)

plan_codes.p2:
left = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name + "_left", "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
left.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
left.sem_filter(
    "the review is overall positive toward the movie",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)

right = PhysicalPipeline(plan_name + "_right", "Reviews.csv", load_data("Reviews.csv"))
right.filter(lambda row: row["idx"] == "ant_man_and_the_wasp_quantumania")
right.sem_filter(
    "the review is overall positive toward the movie",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewText"]
)

joined = left.sem_join(
    right,
    "the two rows are different reviews, and the first reviewId is smaller than the second reviewId",
    model=pz.Model.GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE,
    depends_on=["reviewId"]
)
joined.project(["idx", "reviewId", "reviewId_right"])
joined.limit(10)
joined

cost_model_explanation: The cost model and executions showed that sem_join was the main cost/latency driver, so the winning design reduced join difficulty by first sem-filtering to likely positive reviews. GOOGLE_GEMINI_2_5_FLASH_LITE was the best cost-quality model for both the sentiment filter and the lightweight reviewId ordering join, while the stronger FLASH filter in p3 added cost without improving quality. A direct same-sentiment join over full review text (p4) was cheapest but lost too much quality.
